meta.title: Pricing in 2027 while churn rises
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO and leadership team
meta.purpose: Should Palisade raise prices at 2027 renewals while churn rises, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR 15% with retention above 100%?
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data: the company and all figures are fictional

inputs.label: Briefing pack: Palisade Docs, raise prices while churn is rising?
Choices made on the user's behalf (user unavailable; recommended options taken)
inputs.content: Mode deep deck, 30–40 slides, client diagnostic, navy theme, audience CEO and leadership team approving the plan. Plan parameters: mid-market +12% at renewal (the CFO's rate; the 2024 test at 10% is the nearest evidence); enterprise 7% on capped and 12% on uncapped renewals; SMB +8% on non-promotion renewals from July 2027 if a Q1 test passes, with half of SMB renewals assumed to fall after July; promotion cohort held at today's price through 2027.

storyline.governing_thought: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay: 12% for mid-market, enterprise up to its caps, and SMB only after a test

exec_summary.text: Rising churn comes from 2025 promotion customers reaching full price: they explain 91% of the SMB rise

sub_points.text: SMB churn outside the promotion moved only from 2.0% to 2.1% a month

exec_summary.text: Mid-market has shown it will pay more and enterprise rarely leaves, but SMB pricing is unproven with Inkwell at $9

sub_points.text: Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year

exec_summary.text: The CFO's 12% can add only $7.6M in 2027, and mid-market and enterprise rises alone clear the $98.9M target

sub_points.text: Without any SMB rise, 2027 ARR still reaches about $99.03M

exec_summary.text: Activation is the lever on the promotion cohort's churn, but fixing it cuts SMB churn by up to a third, not half

sub_points.text: Only 41% of promotion customers activated in month one, against 72% elsewhere

exec_summary.text: Approve in December, raise mid-market and enterprise from January, and decide SMB in July

sub_points.text: A Q1 test of +8% on non-promotion SMB renewals gates the July decision

next_steps.action: Approve 12% for mid-market and uncapped enterprise, 7% for capped enterprise, and the SMB test
Agree one churn definition for the board dashboard, by segment and cohort
Send mid-market and enterprise renewal notices at the new prices
Launch the SMB price test and the promotion-cohort onboarding programme
next_steps.owner: CFO and Head of Customer Success

next_steps.action: Review the test and guardrails, and decide the SMB rise

problem.statement: Should Palisade raise prices at 2027 renewals while churn rises, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR 15% with retention above 100%?
problem.decision_maker: CEO, with the leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
success_criteria: ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M
Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall
Each price move rests on evidence for that segment
out_of_scope: New plans, such as a low-cost SMB tier

one_day_answer.situation: Palisade has $86.0M of ARR, strong retention in mid-market and enterprise, and a CFO proposal to raise every price 12% at renewal
one_day_answer.complication: Monthly SMB churn rose from 2.0% to 3.1%, price complaints rose, and Inkwell now sells a $9 plan
one_day_answer.resolution: Raise mid-market and enterprise prices at renewal, test SMB before touching it, and fix activation of the 2025 promotion cohort
